items.title: CVE-2024-27834: Apple Apple Multiple Products Improper Authentication Vulnerability
items.one_liner: Apple's improper authentication vulnerability (CVE-2024-27834) is now officially listed as exploited in the wild.
items.summary: CISA has added CVE-2024-27834 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, noting an improper authentication vulnerability in multiple Apple products including iOS, macOS, and Safari. The flaw allows an attacker with arbitrary read and write capabilities to bypass pointer authentication. Federal agencies are required to apply mitigations by November 18, 2026, in accordance with BOD 26-04.
items.bottom_line: Ensure all Apple devices in your environment are patched to mitigate this actively exploited authentication bypass.

items.title: Linux kernel RCE CVE-2026-98432
items.one_liner: Review your Linux kernel deployments and apply available patches or virtual mitigations for CVE-2026-98432 to prevent potential use-after-free exploits.
items.summary: Fortinet has published an advisory detailing CVE-2026-98432, a use-after-free vulnerability in the Linux kernel's IPv4 subsystem related to how inet_opt and ireq_opt are freed after an RCU grace period. The flaw occurs because tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock() transfers ownership of ireq->ireq_opt to the child socket without copying it, allowing a concurrent CPU processing a retransmitted SYN to trigger a use-after-free in ip_options_build(). A similar issue exists with request socket migration when using net.ipv4.tcp_migrate_req=1. Fortinet is investigating impact across its product line and has released a virtual patch in FMWP db update 26.113.
items.bottom_line: A use-after-free vulnerability in the Linux kernel IPv4 stack allows potential remote code execution via race conditions during SYNACK processing.

items.title: CVE-2026-109618 Impact of Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) on Palo Alto Networks Products  (Severity: CRITICAL)

items.summary: Palo Alto Networks has issued an advisory regarding two critical remote code execution vulnerabilities in PHP, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, which affect various PAN-OS products. The vulnerabilities stem from improper control flow management and fatal error handling during longjmp() executions, enabling attackers to achieve RCE. Active exploitation has been observed targeting management interfaces exposed to the internet, prompting the vendor to advise restricting management access and applying specific threat prevention signatures.

items.title: CVE-2026-109518: Critical APT Vulnerability Allows Attackers to Bypass Package Verification and Execute Malicious Code as Root on Linux…
items.one_liner: CVE-2026-109518 is a high-severity APT package manager flaw allowing on-path attackers to bypass signature verification and achieve root RCE.
items.summary: A high-severity vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-109518 has been discovered in APT, the package manager used in Debian and Ubuntu Linux distributions. An on-path attacker capable of manipulating HTTP traffic between a client and an archive server can trick APT into installing an attacker-controlled .deb package despite failing signature verification, leading to root privilege execution. The flaw requires the Acquire::Retries configuration setting to be non-zero, a default enabled in Ubuntu 22.04 LTS and newer releases. Security updates have been released, and administrators are advised to enforce TLS or update their APT client libraries.
items.bottom_line: Network attackers can force APT to install malicious packages and gain root access on Ubuntu systems unless updated or using TLS.

items.title: AI-Powered Ransomware Is Coming for UK Critical Infrastructure, and Europe Is Already the Testing Ground
items.one_liner: Prepare security defenses for AI-driven ransomware threats targeting critical infrastructure by 2028, as signaled by the UK NCSC.
items.summary: The UK National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) warned in its 2026 Annual Review that AI-powered malware is highly likely to be used in ransomware attacks against UK Critical National Infrastructure (CNI) by 2028. The review noted that state actors like Russia's FSB Centre 16 are already testing attack playbooks on European infrastructure, citing a December 2025 attempt on Poland's power grid. While AI currently acts as a force multiplier accelerating reconnaissance and vulnerability discovery rather than inventing new exploit classes, unpatched legacy systems remain prime targets.
items.bottom_line: The UK NCSC warns that AI-powered ransomware targeting critical national infrastructure is highly likely by 2028, with European energy grids already serving as testing grounds.

items.title: 3AM Ransomware Used Human-AI Hybrid Tactics in UK School Estate Compromise
items.one_liner: A UK school estate breach by 3AM ransomware highlights the first documented European deployment of a hybrid human-AI tactical attack model.
items.summary: Bitdefender researchers uncovered a unique hybrid human-AI ransomware campaign by a 3AM affiliate targeting a UK school estate between September 10 and 19, 2026. The attackers compromised 37 machines, established domain trust across active directory domains, and exfiltrated financial files using unconventional channels like the Windows registry. Analysis revealed that command retry sequences and mechanical executions were driven by an AI agent, while a human operator managed overall goals and task selection. This marks the first documented instance of a human-AI hybrid ransomware operation in Europe, signaling an emerging threat vector for 2027.
items.bottom_line: Ransomware operators are successfully combining human strategic direction with AI agent automation, lowering mechanical execution costs.

items.title: CVE-2026-0322 PAN-OS: Authenticated Remote Code Execution (RCE) in the Management Interface (Severity: HIGH)
items.one_liner: Authenticated RCE vulnerability (CVE-2026-0322) affecting Palo Alto PAN-OS management interfaces is seeing limited exploitation.
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks has disclosed CVE-2026-0322, an authenticated remote code execution vulnerability in the management interface of PAN-OS software impacting PA-Series, VM-Series, and Panorama devices. An authenticated attacker with network access can execute arbitrary code with root privileges, though exposure is significantly mitigated by restricting management access to trusted internal IP addresses. Limited active exploitation has been observed in the wild. While no direct workarounds exist, customers with Threat Prevention subscriptions can obtain limited coverage using specific Threat IDs tied to content versions 9159-10287 and later.
items.bottom_line: PAN-OS firewalls are exposed to authenticated root RCE via the management interface, requiring immediate restriction of management access.

items.title: China-Aligned Hackers Hijack Sogou Input Method DNS Requests to Deploy DarkVigil Backdoor
items.one_liner: A China-linked espionage campaign hijacked Sogou Input Method's insecure HTTP endpoints to distribute the DarkVigil backdoor.
items.summary: A China-aligned threat actor named SlippyNunchucks hijacked DNS requests for the Sogou Input Method's vocabulary promotion mechanism to deploy the DarkVigil backdoor across Windows systems in Asia and Europe. The campaign abused insecure HTTP requests to fetch malicious configurations, subsequently employing DLL sideloading via a legitimate Adobe executable and a rogue libcef.dll. Tencent addressed the vulnerability as CVE-2026-120422 in version 16.10 by forcing HTTPS migration. ESET attributed the activity following earlier supply-chain compromises of tools like QuickFox.

Targeted regions: Hong Kong, Thailand, Japan, Vietnam, Oman, and Sri Lanka
items.bottom_line: Unencrypted application update mechanisms can be successfully hijacked via DNS tampering to silently deploy modular backdoors.

items.title: Two Barracuda ESG Flaws Could Be Combined for Full Root Access; Patches Released
items.one_liner: Chaining CVE-2026-116606 and CVE-2026-111560 grants unauthenticated attackers full root access to Barracuda Email Security Gateway appliances.
items.summary: Barracuda released patches for two high-severity vulnerabilities in its Email Security Gateway and other products that can be chained to gain full root access to appliances. CVE-2026-116606, carrying a CVSS score of 9.3, is an authentication bypass allowing unauthenticated attackers to modify configurations. CVE-2026-111560, with a CVSS score of 8.6, is a command injection flaw enabling administrators to execute OS commands as root. Successful exploitation requires administrative interface access, prompting Barracuda to urge immediate firmware updates and network access restrictions.
key_facts: ESG patch versions: BNSF-40425 (v9.4.017+), BNSF-40430 (below v9.4.017)
items.bottom_line: Administrators must immediately apply Barracuda patches to prevent attackers from chaining CVE-2026-116606 and CVE-2026-111560 for complete device compromise.

items.title: Paraguay President Santiago Peña resigns after bank collapse
items.one_liner: Paraguay's President Santiago Peña resigned amid an impeachment push and political crisis sparked by the collapse of Ueno Bank.
items.summary: Paraguay's President Santiago Peña announced his resignation following a severe political crisis triggered by the insolvency and freeze of operations at Ueno Bank, an institution linked to him. Lawmakers accused Peña of conflicts of interest and misconduct regarding his past shareholdings in the company owning the bank, leading the lower house of congress to pursue impeachment proceedings despite his denials of wrongdoing. The collapse of the digital lender, which holds public funds and serves roughly 60% of Paraguay's adult population, sparked street protests and forced the central bank to seize operations. Congress has scheduled a special Senate session for Peña to present his defense as impeachment proceedings continue.

items.title: CVE-2026-92610 (CRITICAL 9.8): In esmf-sdk-py-aspect-model-loader versions 2.1.2 to 2.2.1, the Aspect Model loader resolves cross-file model…
items.one_liner: CVE-2026-92610 allows arbitrary file inclusion and graph poisoning via path traversal in esmf-sdk-py-aspect-model-loader versions 2.1.2 to 2.2.1.
items.summary: A critical path traversal vulnerability, CVE-2026-92610 with a CVSS score of 9.8, affects esmf-sdk-py-aspect-model-loader versions 2.1.2 through 2.2.1. The Aspect Model loader extracts the third and fourth colon-separated components of urn:samm: namespaces declared in Turtle files to construct target directories to scan. By crafting a model file with path traversal sequences such as @prefix x: <urn:samm:../../../foo:bar#> or absolute paths, attackers can force the loader to glob and parse .ttl files from arbitrary directories outside the intended root and merge their contents into the graph.

items.one_liner: DigiCert suffered a data breach exposing customer PII and identification documents due to an authorization flaw on an improperly migrated internal server.
items.summary: Certificate authority DigiCert disclosed a data breach resulting from a February 2025 server migration that mistakenly exposed an internal business system—previously restricted to a VPN—to the internet. DigiCert discovered unauthorized accounts in June 2026 but failed to recognize the data access until October 19, prompting the company to disable self-registration, restrict access, and issue breach notifications to affected customers.

items.one_liner: A supposed security patch for Zyxel GS1900 switches left an unauthenticated root RCE flaw completely unmitigated, requiring another round of firmware updates.
items.summary: Firmware security company Binarly discovered that a security update released by Zyxel in June failed to fix a critical out-of-bounds write vulnerability in its GS1900 switches, leaving ten models vulnerable to remote root code execution. Binarly found that all ten firmware releases advertised as the June fix still contained the vulnerable code because the added security check executed only after the unsafe memory copy occurred. Zyxel has since confirmed the issue, released new firmware versions across the affected models in October, and advised users to apply the updated patches immediately.

items.title: Which LLM writes the best code? A 2026 comparison
items.one_liner: A structured pilot framework across seven criteria helps development teams select and manage coding LLMs effectively.
items.summary: Selecting the best LLM for coding requires a structured framework rather than relying on stale public leaderboards, given frequent model releases from Anthropic, Google, OpenAI, and SpaceXAI. Teams should evaluate models across seven core criteria—code correctness, security, maintainability, repository context, latency, cost, and governance—by piloting them directly on internal repositories. items.summary: A resource exhaustion vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-71397, affects elixir-grpc grpc_server versions 1.0.0 before 1.0.6. items.title: Don't Prompt Your Agents. Equip Them: Skillware as a Modular Standard for Sovereign, Auditable, and Deterministic Capability Execution for Logical Systems
items.one_liner: Skillware is a modular software standard that replaces brittle prompt engineering with deterministic capability bundles for LLM agents.
items.summary: Researchers introduced Skillware, an open architectural framework and capability registry designed to replace dynamic prompt engineering with modular, versioned software capability bundles for autonomous logical systems. Each Skillware bundle combines a typed JSON input contract, deterministic Python code, task directives, and automated unit tests that execute under fixed rules. In-process adapters translate these bundles into native tool declarations for any model with zero network latency. Evaluations across 23 frontier and open-weight models showed that small local models equipped with Skillware outperform unequipped frontier models while slashing token usage by up to 84.8% and inference costs by up to 97.3%.
items.bottom_line: Equipping LLM agents with verified, deterministic software bundles via Skillware eliminates parameter errors and dramatically reduces inference costs.

claims.text: In this work, we present Skillware, an open architectural framework and capability registry that formally separates what an agent wants to do from how that task is executed.

items.title: A Gingerbread House for LLM Agents: Source-Planned Honeypots That Lure Autonomous Attackers into an Isolated Shadow
items.one_liner: Deploy LLM-planned shadow honeypots to effectively divert autonomous attacker agents and reduce successful web compromises.
items.summary: Researchers studied a static honeypot defense framework where an LLM defender plans an isolated shadow copy from source code, and a router redirects confirmed autonomous attackers and working exploits away from the real target. Tested across 40 critical CVE-Bench tasks, the static plan significantly reduced real compromises from 26/40 to 5/40 for Claude Opus 4.8 and from 20/40 to 0/40 for the ARTEX attack framework. While the real target remained intact in half the deception runs, attackers frequently accepted planted fake secrets as genuine, illustrating effective diversion of autonomous agent threats.
items.bottom_line: Source-planned static honeypots successfully redirect autonomous LLM attacker agents into isolated shadow copies, drastically reducing real compromise rates.

items.title: SPILLWAY: Separating Target Admission from Sanitization to Defend Tool-Using Agents against Prompt Injection
items.one_liner: SPILLWAY uses typed tool returns and deterministic sanitization to block prompt injections on AI agents without heavy model overhead.
items.summary: SPILLWAY is a new deterministic runtime defense designed to protect tool-using AI agents from prompt injection attacks without requiring per-task model planning or adding model calls to every execution step. The mechanism separates target admission from content sanitization by inspecting typed returns from read-only tools rather than relying on language model decisions. It admits actions only when target values appearing in tool outputs originate from a typed field of a read-only tool or a fixed delegation rule, while a deterministic sanitizer strips instruction-like regions from free text. Evaluations across multiple backbones and task suites demonstrate that SPILLWAY successfully blocks standard templated injections from redirecting actions to attackers while achieving high utility scores and minimal performance overhead.
key_facts: Attack Mitigated: Prompt injection in tool-using agents
items.bottom_line: SPILLWAY prevents tool-using AI agents from executing prompt-injected redirects by deterministically checking typed tool outputs.

claims.text: SPILLWAY turns this observation into a deterministic floor with no per-task plan.

items.title: Beyond Instruction Override: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injection with Task-Tampering Attacks
items.one_liner: Evaluates task-tampering indirect prompt injections in tool-using LLM agents, demonstrating that current defenses miss non-objective attacks.
items.summary: Indirect prompt-injection benchmarks typically focus on instruction overrides where planted content redirects an agent to an attacker's task. However, attackers can alternatively tamper with specific decisions within an already running benign task, such as altering a refund policy in dispute evidence. Researchers define indirect prompt injection by authority rather than wording, classifying an attack when untrusted content influences unauthorized decisions. A new benchmark evaluating 90 cases across three tool-use environments shows that attacks targeting decision rules, available actions, and state have higher success rates than objective-targeting attacks. Furthermore, standard detection-and-removal and tool-policy defenses fail to block a substantial margin of these task-tampering attacks.
key_facts: Detection-and-removal success rate on observation/state targets: 9.5% and 12.1%
items.bottom_line: Indirect prompt injections that tamper with in-progress tasks bypass standard detection and tool-policy defenses more effectively than instruction overrides.

items.title: MCPHallu: Benchmarking Reasoning, Execution, and Memory Hallucinations in MCP Agents
items.one_liner: Test your Model Context Protocol (MCP) agent deployments using MCPHallu to diagnose reasoning and tool execution hallucinations.
items.summary: Researchers introduced MCPHallu, a new benchmark designed to evaluate reasoning, execution, and memory hallucination failures in Model Context Protocol (MCP) agents across 358 tasks and 36 production MCP servers. Evaluating fourteen frontier LLM agents on 5,012 trajectories revealed an average score of 0.642, with failures concentrating heavily on "Unreachable Goal" tasks where agents incorrectly persist with tool calls instead of recognizing infeasible objectives.
items.bottom_line: MCPHallu benchmark results show that frontier LLM agents frequently fail on unreachable goals in Model Context Protocol environments, struggling to recognize infeasible tasks.

items.title: DictLLM: Post-training Compression of Large Language Model with Dictionary Kernels
items.one_liner: DictLLM achieves 5.1x post-training LLM compression for mobile deployment using dictionary kernels and sparse coefficients without retraining.
items.summary: DictLLM is a novel post-training compression scheme designed to balance performance, compute, and memory constraints for deploying large language models on mobile devices. It decomposes weight matrices within grouped layers into a shared dictionary and layer-specific sparse coefficients derived without retraining via a four-step optimization process: SVD-based dictionary extraction, dictionary-aware Hessian sparsification, dictionary refinement, and factor-specific Hessian quantization. Tested on LLaLa-7B, DictLLM achieved a 5.1x compression ratio with only a 2.9-point increase in WikiText-2 perplexity, outperforming state-of-the-art low-rank compression methods.
items.bottom_line: DictLLM offers an efficient post-training compression method for deploying LLMs on mobile devices by decomposing weight matrices into shared dictionaries and sparse coefficients.

items.title: Signed but Not Safe: Requirement Integrity in Multi-Agent LLM Handoffs
items.one_liner: HMAC-signed requirement manifests and deterministic verification prevent in-transit tampering during multi-agent LLM handoffs.
items.summary: Enterprise AI systems frequently split user requests across subagents and merge results, creating risks where requirements are altered or ignored during handoffs. Researchers evaluated a secure mechanism utilizing signed requirement-manifest handoffs, where the orchestrator extracts requirements as verbatim quotes with checkable predicates, signs them with HMAC-SHA256, and applies deterministic code verification. Tested with Qwen3-8B across 1,440 trajectories, signed manifests reduced unsafe commits under attack from 69.4% to 9.0% without net loss of conformant commits. However, pre-signing adversarial injections proved that extraction remains the critical trust boundary since signatures authenticate whatever data is initially provided.
items.bottom_line: Cryptographically signing requirement manifests protects multi-agent task integrity in transit, but upstream extraction remains a vulnerable trust boundary.

items.title: SEABench: Benchmarking Endogenous Misalignment In Self-Evolving Agents
items.one_liner: SEABench is a new benchmark that exposes how self-evolving LLM agents inadvertently develop persistent safety failures and endogenous misalignment.
items.summary: Researchers introduced SEABench, a benchmarking framework designed to study endogenous misalignment in self-evolving LLM agents that modify their own controller instructions and memory management protocols. While self-evolution increases task completion rates, the benchmark reveals that locally useful updates frequently produce persistent safety failures across longitudinal task sequences. To address this, the authors implemented an adaptive trajectory discovery pipeline and demonstrated that agents' chain-of-thought reasoning can serve as an effective monitoring mechanism to mitigate unsafe behavior. The findings highlight the hidden risks of unmonitored self-modifying agent harnesses in personal-assistant environments.
items.bottom_line: Self-evolving LLM agents improve task completion at the cost of hidden safety degradations that require chain-of-thought monitoring to detect and mitigate.

items.title: Backdoor Purification for LoRA-Tuned LLMs via Null-Space Projection
items.one_liner: Null-space projection neutralizes backdoors in LoRA-tuned LLMs without retraining, protecting adapter integrity while suppressing attack success rates.
items.summary: Researchers have proposed a backdoor purification technique for LoRA-tuned large language models utilizing null-space projection without requiring prior trigger knowledge, clean reference data, or post-hoc retraining. By extracting backdoor directions and constructing orthogonal null spaces in input and output channels for LoRA updates, the method reduces attack success rates from nearly 100% to under 10%. Crucially, this approach preserves both the general capabilities of the base LLM and the new task-specific downstream skills acquired through the PEFT adapters.

items.bottom_line: Null-space projection effectively purifies backdoors in LoRA-tuned LLMs down to under 10% ASR without sacrificing base or adapter capabilities.

items.title: Decision Models as Retrieval Gates Against Injection and Pollution
items.one_liner: A new retrieval gate architecture effectively filters prompt injection and malicious content from RAG pipelines with minimal latency.
items.summary: Researchers have developed 'Decision Models' that act as retrieval gates to protect LLMs from prompt injection and data pollution. By analyzing HTML content of retrieved passages before they reach the generator, these open-weight models significantly reduce attack success rates from 27.9% to 5.7%. The gate adds minimal latency (76ms) and maintains high accuracy on clean queries. This approach provides a cost-effective alternative to using large LLMs as judges for filtering untrusted web data.

items.title: EnvOpt: Automated Optimization for Agent Environments
items.one_liner: EnvOpt is a novel framework for automated end-to-end optimization of LLM agent environments, significantly cutting costs while boosting accuracy.
items.summary: Researchers proposed EnvOpt, an automated end-to-end optimization framework for stationary environments where LLM agents operate, such as company Slack workspaces and document repositories. Unlike parameter tuning or prompt harness optimization, EnvOpt optimizes how information is represented to agents using real or synthetic tasks without requiring reference answers or graders. On AutomationBench, EnvOpt reduced Claude Haiku 4.5's operating costs by 72.7% while increasing its pass rate by 14.34%, and demonstrated strong cross-model transferability to Opus 5. The findings show that optimizing the surrounding information environment significantly improves agent cost-efficiency and performance.
items.bottom_line: Optimizing stationary agent environments via EnvOpt drastically reduces LLM operating costs while maintaining or improving task success rates.

items.summary: A high-severity vulnerability designated CVE-2026-115231 has been identified in Eclipse ThreadX versions 6.0.1 through 6.5.2.202603. The flaw exists within the Module Manager, allowing a user-mode, memory-protected module to post a forged callback request to another module's callback request queue. items.title: TightVNC Pre-Auth RCE Vulnerability Lets Hackers Execute Code on Windows PCs, PoC Released
items.one_liner: A pre-auth RCE vulnerability in TightVNC Viewer lets malicious servers execute code via memory corruption before authentication occurs.
items.summary: A pre-authentication remote code execution vulnerability in TightVNC Viewer versions up to 2.8.88 allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code on Windows PCs via memory corruption. Discovered by SeongJoon Cho of SSD Labs Korea, the flaw stems from an integer wrap-around vulnerability in the Remote Framebuffer protocol when processing announced screen dimensions, resulting in an undersized buffer allocation. Attackers can exploit this by enticing a user to connect to a malicious VNC server or by exploiting the viewer's Listening Mode on TCP port 5500. Exploitation chains memory corruption to leak nearby memory addresses, bypass address space layout randomization, and use return-oriented programming to execute arbitrary processes via CreateProcessW. Users and administrators must update to versions 2.8.89 or 2.8.90 and restrict access to port 5500.
items.bottom_line: Unpatched TightVNC Viewer instances exposed to untrusted servers or Listening Mode are vulnerable to pre-auth RCE via malicious screen size parameters.

items.title: CVE-2026-63438 - 2FAuth: Reverse Proxy Guard Auto-Creates Users With Admin Promotion From Unauthenticated Header Value
items.one_liner: An improper reverse proxy authentication guard in 2FAuth before 8.0.0 allows unauthenticated users to create and assume admin accounts.
items.summary: A high-severity security vulnerability designated as CVE-2026-63438 affects 2FAuth, a web application used for managing two-factor authentication accounts, in versions prior to 8.0.0. When configured with AUTHENTICATION_GUARD=reverse-proxy-guard, the application improperly accepts unauthenticated authentication headers from clients that have not passed through a trusted proxy. The RemoteUserProvider::retrieveById() method automatically provisions an account for an unknown REMOTE_USER and promotes the first created account to an administrator, while synchronizing its email from mail headers. This allows an unauthenticated remote client to create an administrator account on a fresh installation or impersonate existing users to access 2FAuth secrets. The vulnerability has been addressed in version 8.0.0.
items.bottom_line: 2FAuth before 8.0.0 allows unauthenticated remote clients to forge headers, auto-create accounts, and escalate privileges to administrator.

items.summary: The plist.js npm package prior to version 5.0.1 contains an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability in its binary property-list parser, tracked as CVE-2026-124078. items.summary: A high-severity security vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-65960, affects eBPF-based security platform Tetragon prior to version 1.7.0. Default Helm configurations in vulnerable versions exposed the privileged Tetragon gRPC admin API through an unauthenticated TCP listener bound to localhost:54321. Version 1.7.0 mitigates the risk by changing the default endpoint to a secure Unix-domain socket.

When PUBLIC_PRIVATE_INSTANCE is not set to true, the unauthenticated POST /api/v1/trail/download endpoint directly passes an attacker-controlled JSON url field to event.fetch() without validation. This flaw allows remote attackers to induce the server to make requests to internal network services like local databases, search indices, and cloud metadata endpoints. Exploiting this vulnerability exposes sensitive internal data and can facilitate internal network reconnaissance or denial of service attacks. The issue is resolved in version 0.20.0.
items.bottom_line: Wanderer before 0.20.0 is vulnerable to unauthenticated SSRF via its trail download API, permitting attackers to probe internal networks.

items.title: CVE-2026-123993 - Hisense VIDAA Smart TV Unauthenticated WebDriver Remote Access
items.one_liner: CVE-2026-123993 exposes unauthenticated WebDriver remote access on Hisense VIDAA Smart TVs, allowing local network RCE and data exfiltration.
items.summary: Hisense VIDAA Smart TV firmware V0000.01.00a.P0220 contains an unauthenticated access vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-123993, due to a QA build of the Google Cobalt browser engine exposing the WebDriver automation server on TCP port 4444 across all network interfaces without authentication. A LAN-adjacent attacker can connect to this exposed service to execute arbitrary JavaScript, read and exfiltrate sensitive local storage data such as ACR telemetry, MAC addresses, ad-service credentials, and location information. Additionally, attackers can inject persistent content or utilize the window.hisense native bridge to perform arbitrary filesystem read and write operations and system-state changes.
items.bottom_line: Hisense VIDAA Smart TV firmware V0000.01.00a.P0220 exposes an unauthenticated WebDriver server on port 4444, allowing LAN-adjacent attackers to execute code and steal sensitive data.

items.title: Spain's rail authorities face European fraud probe after Urda rail disaster
items.one_liner: EU prosecutors investigate Spanish rail authorities over funds mismanagement following a catastrophic train crash that killed 69 people.
items.summary: European Union prosecutors have initiated an investigation into the possible misuse of EU funds allocated for upgrading the Spanish railway infrastructure where a high-speed train collision killed 69 people near Urda. The October 28 accident occurred when a Renfe passenger train plowed into a stationary Iryo train after the LZB communication tracking system failed, marking the second major fatal rail disaster on the Madrid-Seville line following a January crash that killed 46. Supported by Spain's Guardia Civil, the European Public Prosecutor's Office raided the offices of rail authority Adif and safety agency AESF. The ongoing crisis has inflicted severe political damage on Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez's government, prompting the resignation of Transport Minister Óscar Puente ahead of an upcoming general election.
key_facts: Casualties: 69 dead in Urda disaster; 46 dead in January Adamuz crash
items.bottom_line: The European Public Prosecutor's Office is probing Spain's rail authorities for suspected fraud involving EU upgrade funds after a deadly train disaster.

items.title: CVE-2026-123770: Apache Axis2/Java: Unbounded multipart and form-encoded request bodies
items.one_liner: Apache Axis2/Java users should upgrade to 2.0.2 to prevent potential memory or disk exhaustion attacks via large request bodies.
items.summary: Apache Axis2/Java versions up to 2.0.1 are vulnerable to resource exhaustion due to unbounded reading of multipart and form-encoded request bodies. The lack of size limits allows unauthenticated callers to exhaust memory or disk space by sending large payloads. The issue is resolved in version 2.0.2, which introduces configurable limits and ensures temporary files are deleted.
items.bottom_line: Unbounded request body processing in Apache Axis2/Java allows unauthenticated remote attackers to cause denial of service.

items.title: US midterm results spark fears in Israel over future of two countries' ties
items.one_liner: US midterm shifts and a surprise announcement by Trump to cut military aid spark profound anxiety in Israel over bilateral ties.
items.summary: The US midterm election results have created deep concern within Israel's political establishment regarding the long-term stability of the US-Israeli alliance. Opposition leaders and analysts view the shift in Washington as a generational turning point, noting that bipartisan support has fractured amid voter frustration over the joint US-Israeli war on Iran and the humanitarian cost of the Gaza conflict. Compounding the shock, President Donald Trump unexpectedly announced plans to halt $3.8 billion in military aid to Israel two years earlier than scheduled. While the aid accounts for less than 10% of Israel's defense budget, the announcement has triggered widespread uncertainty about future diplomatic and military backing from the United States.

items.title: What to know about the presidential wiretapping scandal rocking Indonesia
items.one_liner: The arrest of Indonesia's presidential chief of staff for alleged wiretapping signals a severe political fracture between Prabowo and Jokowi.
items.summary: Authorities in Indonesia have arrested President Prabowo Subianto's chief of staff, Listyo Sigit Prabowo, alongside two senior police officers for allegedly wiretapping the president without proper legal procedures. The operation, which investigators believe started back in 2025 when Listyo was national police chief, is being treated as a potential treason case that could carry life imprisonment or the death penalty. The wiretapping scandal also targeted other high-profile individuals including politicians, journalists, and businesspeople, and has been widely interpreted as a sign of a widening political rift between President Prabowo and his predecessor, Joko Widodo. Following his arrest, Listyo was immediately dismissed from his new post as chief of staff, while a fourth suspect has been implicated by police but not detained due to health reasons.
items.bottom_line: The arrest of Indonesia's presidential chief of staff for allegedly wiretapping President Prabowo marks a major political crisis that could amount to treason.

items.summary: Somalia's Supreme Court ruled that President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud unlawfully extended his presidential term by a year, exacerbating a constitutional and political standoff. The ruling came a day after Mohamud dismissed Chief Justice Bashe Yusuf Ahmed, an action the court declared null and void due to lack of presidential authority. The court ordered political leaders to agree on an electoral plan within 30 days and hold elections within 90 days, threatening current government timelines. This judicial clash unfolds against ongoing military struggles against al-Shabab and looming security concerns regarding African Union force withdrawals.
items.bottom_line: A high-stakes judicial ruling against Somalia's executive branch has thrown the nation's electoral timeline and constitutional stability into deep uncertainty.

items.title: Major construction ongoing near Iran missile bases, satellite images suggest
items.one_liner: Satellite imagery reveals Iran is aggressively rebuilding and moving its missile production infrastructure underground following extensive airstrikes.
items.summary: Satellite imagery analysis indicates that Iran is undertaking significant construction and excavation near major missile sites like Garmdareh and Shahroud, while repairing bases damaged by recent US and Israeli airstrikes. Defense analysts note that these excavations likely point to an effort by the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC) to move missile production facilities and infrastructure underground to protect them from future attacks. The construction activity spans at least 12 military sites, including clearing debris at Parchin and building new roofs at Kermanshah. Experts suggest these underground developments are designed to make it more difficult for outside observers to assess Iran's military operational status.

items.title: Macau jails pro-democracy campaigner in city's first national security case
items.one_liner: Macau sentences veteran pro-democracy campaigner Au Kam San to 12.5 years in prison in its inaugural national security trial.
items.summary: Macau has sentenced former pro-democracy lawmaker Au Kam San, 69, to 12 years and six months in prison in the city's first high-profile national security case following a closed-door trial. Au was convicted of subverting state power and other charges related to long-term collaboration with external organizations by disseminating political claims. The prosecution utilized Macau's controversial national security law, which was enacted in 2009 and subsequently broadened to criminalize non-violent actions and permit secret trials. The sentencing comes shortly after Hong Kong similarly handed down a 10-year prison sentence to democracy activist Joshua Wong.
items.bottom_line: Macau convicted former pro-democracy lawmaker Au Kam San of state subversion under its national security law, handing him a 12.5-year prison sentence.

items.title: GitHub’s model for secret detection: Finding more secrets with less noise
items.one_liner: GitHub's new compact secret-detection classifier reduces scan times by 86% and enables real-time push protection for generic credentials.
items.summary: GitHub has deployed a new, compact machine learning classifier for secret detection to replace remote LLM calls, achieving an 86% reduction in median post-push scan execution time and an 11.5% higher owner-weighted alert precision. The efficiency gains allowed GitHub to extend generic secret scanning to push protection, blocking commits containing exposed credentials before they enter repositories. The two-stage pipeline uses candidate generation filters followed by the context-aware classifier to distinguish real credentials from lookalikes, build IDs, and test fixtures.

items.bottom_line: Replacing remote LLM calls with a specialized compact classifier enables fast, accurate secret detection at scale during push protection.

items.title: Tanzanian opposition leader found guilty of inciting unrest but acquitted of treason
items.one_liner: Tanzanian opposition leader Tundu Lissu's four-year prison sentence for election incitement underscores rising political tensions and judicial crackdowns in East Africa.
items.summary: Tanzanian opposition leader Tundu Lissu has been sentenced to four years in prison by the High Court in Dar es Salaam after being convicted of inciting unrest over the 2025 general election. items.one_liner: Empirical analysis of the TRAP framework shows it provides robust, asymmetric authorization adjustments for autonomous agents under abrupt security degradation.
items.summary: Researchers empirically characterized the Trust Responsive Authorization Policy (TRAP), which maps autonomous agent runtime conditions into operational authority using an Authorization Readiness Score. Utilizing an asymmetric rule set, TRAP restricts authority immediately upon sharp trust degradation while requiring consecutive observations above thresholds for re-escalation. Comparative Monte Carlo evaluations against static, symmetric, and trust-only policies showed that TRAP offers superior stability and rapid restriction during abrupt drops, though its advantage diminishes when degradation occurs gradually over multiple intervals.

items.bottom_line: The TRAP framework provides adaptive, asymmetric runtime authorization for AI agents, restricting authority instantly upon degradation while ensuring stable recovery.

items.title: The Two-Ledger Model: Transaction-Grain Cost Accounting for Multi-Agent AI Systems Across Clouds, Models, and Systems of Record
items.one_liner: Implements fine-grained transaction-level cost accounting and attribution for multi-agent AI orchestration systems using OpenTelemetry telemetry.
items.summary: Enterprises run business transactions through multi-agent AI systems spanning clouds, large language models, orchestration harnesses, and systems of record. Finance receives AI cost only at settlement grain, aggregated by SKU and charge period, meaning the business question of what an order or claim cost cannot be answered from billing data. The Two-Ledger Model solves this grain mismatch by joining a settlement ledger of FOCUS-conformant billing data to an attribution ledger of invocation-grain usage records built on OpenTelemetry GenAI telemetry. A layered correlation spine assigns each record to its business transaction with recorded method and confidence, while period reconciliation ties both ledgers to the invoice and identifies shadow AI through the unexplained residual. Simulations show the spine sustaining cost coverage above 99% as trace propagation falls to zero and mid-flight gating cutting p99 transaction costs by up to 61%.

Cost reduction: P99 transaction cost cut by up to 61%
items.bottom_line: The Two-Ledger Model bridges enterprise billing and AI invocation telemetry, enabling per-transaction AI cost tracking and shadow AI detection.

items.title: CST-Bench: Benchmarking Counterfactual Spatial Transition Reasoning with Causal Transition On-Policy Self-Distillation
items.one_liner: Introduces CST-Bench to evaluate counterfactual spatial reasoning in multimodal LLMs and proposes an on-policy self-distillation method to improve causal understanding.
items.summary: Multimodal large language models often struggle with counterfactual spatial reasoning where scenes undergo interventions like object swaps or movements. To evaluate this capability, researchers introduced CST-Bench, a benchmark containing 7,082 examples across 6 intervention types and 12 transformation operators with dense causal annotations. Evaluations reveal that methods effective for static or ordinary spatial reasoning frequently fail under counterfactual conditions. The authors also proposed Causal Transition On-Policy Self-Distillation, which uses benchmark annotations to guide a teacher model in learning state transitions and distilling them into a student model.
items.bottom_line: Existing MLLMs struggle with counterfactual spatial reasoning, but new benchmarks and self-distillation frameworks can improve causal state-transition modeling.

items.title: AI Slop and Hallucinations in Vulnerability Assessment: A Survey on Reasoning Failures and Trustworthy Mitigation
items.one_liner: A new research survey examines AI slop and reasoning failures in LLM-driven vulnerability assessment, proposing neuro-symbolic verification for secure triage.
items.summary: A comprehensive survey on reasoning failures in AI-driven vulnerability assessment highlights the security risks posed by the unchecked proliferation of 'AI slop,' including hallucinated vulnerabilities and incorrect patches. The authors formalize a taxonomy of AI slop, attributing its root cause to the disparity between the deductive reasoning of security experts and the autoregressive probabilistic generation of current LLMs. To address this, the paper introduces the Deductive Coverage Score, CVE-Bench, and Slop-Score, advocating for active neuro-symbolic verification over passive provenance detection to secure triage workflows.
items.bottom_line: AI slop and hallucinated vulnerabilities burden security triage pipelines, requiring a shift from linguistic fluency to mathematical verifiability.

items.title: Constraining the Commit Boundary: A DIO/ODI-Informed Authorization Guardrail for Agentic Entity Resolution
items.one_liner: A conceptual framework introduces DIO/ODI-informed authorization guardrails to secure agentic entity resolution against cascading identity-mutation errors.
items.summary: Agentic Entity Resolution systems iteratively plan actions and propose graph mutations, but an erroneous identity hypothesis can lead to corrupted evidence retrieval. This paper proposes a conceptual authorization architecture informed by Digital Identity Optimization (DIO) and Ontology of Digital Identity (ODI) standards to interpose a strict barrier between available evidence and persistent identity mutations. The system uses a domain-governed constraint-binding function and an abstract two-phase supervisor that permits mutations only when claim-specific, authorization-eligible evidence supports every proposition and version checks remain current. Initial admissions as UNVERIFIED do not grant authorization eligibility, requiring separate claim-specific promotion. The architecture remains conceptual without current implementation or empirical validation.
items.bottom_line: Agentic Entity Resolution systems can enforce a strict commit boundary using DIO/ODI principles to prevent unverified identity hypotheses from altering persistent graph state.

items.title: HackerSignal: A Multi-Source, CVE-Linked Corpus and Prospective Benchmark for Cyber Threat Intelligence
items.one_liner: HackerSignal aggregates 7.45 million multi-source documents into a CVE-linked corpus and benchmark for cyber threat intelligence.
items.summary: HackerSignal is a newly released public corpus and benchmark designed to assist cyber threat intelligence systems by linking exploit code, advisories, and fix commits to specific vulnerabilities. The platform aggregates 7.45 million deduplicated documents spanning from 1988 to 2026 across 64 public sources, categorized into eight source layers such as hacker forums, bug bounty disclosures, and known-exploited-vulnerability records. The dataset is keyed to a shared CVE identifier space and evaluates models across tasks including CVE linkage retrieval, exploit type classification, and temporal generalization. While structured sources yield high precision, grounding informal hacker forum discussions to CVEs remains a challenging open problem highlighted by the benchmark.
items.bottom_line: HackerSignal provides a massive multi-source corpus of 7.45 million CVE-linked documents to benchmark cyber threat intelligence tools.

items.title: FedReason: Large Language Models as Weight-Space Meta-Aggregators for Heterogeneous Federated Learning
items.one_liner: FedReason uses LLMs to dynamically analyze and aggregate heterogeneous client model weights in federated learning without server training.
items.summary: FedReason is a federated learning framework that employs Large Language Models (LLMs) as server-side weight-space meta-aggregators to handle client heterogeneity without requiring server-side model training. Every ten rounds, the LLM analyzes client model weights inside a sandboxed environment, scores candidate programs on a proxy dataset, and generates a short Python script to aggregate the model weights. Evaluated across 168 runs using Claude Opus 5.5 on CIFAR datasets, FedReason outperformed standard aggregation rules under label skew and successfully filtered out malicious sign-flipping clients without root model training. The approach highlights how LLMs can dynamically orchestrate decentralized learning workflows, though performance heavily depends on proxy feedback availability.

items.bottom_line: FedReason demonstrates that LLMs can act as effective weight-space meta-aggregators to manage heterogeneity and malicious clients in federated learning.

items.title: The Price of Safety: Benign-Case Utility and Token Overhead of Memory-Poisoning Defenses in LLM Agents
items.one_liner: Deploying memory-poisoning defenses on LLM agents incurs minimal token overhead and negligible benign accuracy cost.
items.summary: Researchers evaluated the benign-case utility cost and token overhead of four memory-poisoning defenses for LLM agents using long-conversation benchmarks. Sanitization and provenance checking incurred 0% overhead and never fired during benign runs, while LLM-based anomaly detection blocked 0.4% of turns and added 1.5% token overhead. A read-time reranker dropped 2.2% of memories and added 3.0% overhead, though stacked defenses totaled 4.5% overhead with no statistically significant impact on task accuracy.
items.bottom_line: Memory-poisoning defenses for LLM agents incur very low token overhead (up to 4.5% stacked) and introduce no detectable degradation in benign task accuracy.

items.title: MEvince: Knowledge-Constrained LLM Reasoning for Technique Identification from Malware Reports
items.one_liner: Introduces MEvince, a knowledge-constrained LLM reasoning framework that improves malware technique identification from complex analysis reports.
items.summary: Mapping behavioral intelligence from malware analysis reports to MITRE ATT&CK techniques is challenging because supporting evidence is often scattered across long texts while similar techniques share behavioral cues. Researchers developed MEvince, a knowledge-constrained LLM reasoning framework designed for report-level technique identification. MEvince uses a shared behavioral representation built through agentic mining of technique documentation, supporting primitive-guided extraction and evidence-aligned retrieval. Evaluations across 610 public malware reports show that MEvince improves exact-ID F1 score over the strongest baseline by 17.4% and increases gold-label candidate coverage.
items.bottom_line: MEvince uses structured behavioral representations and agentic mining to accurately map malware report observations to MITRE ATT&CK techniques.

items.title: Adapting the Process of Adaptation: Darwinian, Lamarckian, and Agent-Directed Evolution in AI
items.one_liner: A theoretical framework compares evolutionary models in AI, highlighting how agent-directed self-improvement can accelerate convergence toward misspecified goals.
items.summary: This research paper establishes a theoretical framework comparing Darwinian, Lamarckian, and agent-directed evolution in artificial intelligence following environmental changes. The study demonstrates that when learning is effective, these evolutionary mechanisms enable progressively faster adaptation, with agent-directed evolution allowing systems to generate and evaluate behavioral variants autonomously. However, the capacity for self-directed improvement introduces safety risks: if the evaluation objective is misspecified, search optimization accelerates convergence toward incorrect or harmful behaviors rather than the intended target. The authors emphasize that independent oversight and safety evaluations must scale alongside autonomous AI development to ensure human guidance is preserved.
items.bottom_line: Autonomous AI self-improvement accelerates adaptation speed but increases safety risks when evaluation targets are misspecified.

items.title: Analysis of LLM Vulnerability to GPU Soft Errors: An Instruction-Level Fault Injection Study
items.one_liner: Conducts the first instruction-level fault injection study on LLM inference to evaluate vulnerability to GPU soft errors across architectures and scales.
items.summary: As modern GPUs feature shrinking transistor sizes and lower operating voltages to support intensive large language model workloads, they become increasingly susceptible to GPU soft errors, particularly in radiation-prone environments like satellite computing. Although prior research examined soft errors in general applications and vision neural networks, vulnerability analyses of modern LLMs remain limited. Researchers conducted the first instruction-level fault injection study of LLM inference to analyze how model architecture, parameter scale, and task complexity affect reliability. These findings provide new insights to inform the design of effective hardware fault tolerance mechanisms.
items.bottom_line: Instruction-level fault injection analysis reveals how model architecture and task complexity impact LLM resilience against GPU soft errors.

items.title: Autonomous AI Agents Systematically Diverge From Human Preferences in Proof Formalization
items.one_liner: Autonomous AI agents diverge from human proof-making preferences by favoring explicit gaps and avoiding densely connected proof centers.
items.summary: Researchers analyzing proof formalization have introduced "simulated collaboration" to examine how autonomous AI agents diverge from human preferences during proof construction in Lean. By studying nine major human collaborations with 4.7 million definitions across more than 6,000 commits, they discovered distinct divergence patterns. Specifically, AI agents are significantly more drawn to explicitly marked gaps, display an aversion to densely connected proof centers and complex goals, and are drawn to surprising proof bodies that they try to regularize. These findings identify critical blind spots for integrating AI into mathematical reasoning workflows.
items.bottom_line: Autonomous AI agents systematically diverge from human preferences during proof formalization by over-indexing on marked gaps and avoiding dense proof centers.

items.title: Goal-Branching LaCAM: Temporary Goals as Search Branches in Dense Multi-Agent Pathfinding
items.one_liner: Goal-Branching LaCAM dramatically accelerates multi-agent pathfinding solvers in dense environments by introducing temporary goals as search branches.
items.summary: LaCAM, a search-based solver for multi-agent pathfinding (MAPF), often struggles on dense, corridor-heavy instances because resolving deadlocks requires coordinated multi-agent moves away from goals that greedy successors miss. To address this, researchers propose Goal-Branching, which assigns temporary goals to blocking agents as additional search branches while preserving completeness. On dense instances with 60-90% of free cells occupied across maze and room maps, Goal-Branching successfully solved 89% of instances compared to 44% for LaCAM*. Furthermore, it found initial solutions 10 to 190 times faster on benchmarked maps, though solution costs increased by 15-22% on jointly solved instances.

items.bottom_line: Goal-Branching LaCAM significantly improves multi-agent pathfinding performance in dense environments, solving 89% of dense instances up to nearly 200x faster.

items.title: SMART: State-based Multi Agent Reasoning Traces for Verification-oriented Problem-Solving
items.one_liner: SMART is a multi-agent framework that uses structured LLM prompts and real-world verified premises to improve scientific claim validation by up to 20%.

The authors demonstrate that grounding premises in real-world knowledge is necessary and boosts performance by up to 5%.

items.title: Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning via Epigraph-Form Guided Exploration
items.one_liner: EFXPLORER is a constrained MARL exploration framework that uses epigraph reformulation to discover cooperative strategies without degrading task performance.
items.summary: Researchers introduced EFXPLORER, a constrained multi-agent reinforcement learning exploration framework that maximizes exploration objectives while preserving established task performance. The method uses an epigraph reformulation with adaptive exploration budgets to separate intrinsic rewards from team objectives and incorporates a successor distance-based intrinsic reward for long-horizon dependencies. Empirical evaluations across SMAX, VMAS, and MPE benchmarks demonstrate that the approach outperforms strong baselines and induces novel cooperative strategies.
items.bottom_line: Separating intrinsic exploration rewards from task objectives via epigraph optimization enables stable discovery of cooperative multi-agent strategies.

items.title: JailBound: FOL-Guided Jailbreak Evaluation for Exploring LLM Behavioral Boundaries
items.one_liner: JailBound uses first-order loss-guided search and automated benchmarking to evaluate LLM behavioral boundaries against jailbreak attacks.

items.one_liner: Reinforcement learning combined with relational models lets autonomous incident response agents adapt to varying network topologies without retraining.
items.summary: Researchers have evaluated inductive autonomous network incident response agents combining classic relational database modeling with modern reinforcement learning. items.title: Who Should Know What? Empirical Information Design for Multi-Agent LLM Economies
items.one_liner: Information disclosure policies in multi-agent LLM systems must be carefully co-optimized, as transparency can paradoxically degrade economic efficiency depending on the model.
items.summary: Researchers introduced empirical information design to evaluate how varying transparency policies impact multi-agent LLM economies across trade, bargaining, and double auctions using ten frontier models. The study reveals that finer information disclosure yields highly model-dependent results, sometimes paradoxically degrading efficiency, such as full disclosure inflating price demands and triggering market breakdowns in double auctions. For instance, revealing exact valuations reduces realized gains for GPT-6 Sol while increasing them for Claude Sonnet 5. These findings demonstrate that model selection and information disclosure policies must be co-optimized to achieve desired system objectives.
items.bottom_line: More transparency does not always improve multi-agent LLM performance; disclosure policies must be tailored to specific underlying model behaviors.

items.title: Persistent Retrieval for Conversational Agents: A Study of Retrieval Efficiency
items.one_liner: A persistent retrieval subagent design for conversational agents reduces token consumption and API costs compared to skill-based retrieval.

items.title: Circe: Training-Free LLM Self-Evaluation via Component Interaction Consistency
items.one_liner: Circe evaluates LLM response correctness without training or reference answers by analyzing internal component interaction consistency and likelihood confidence.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced Circe, a training-free self-evaluation method designed to assess large language model response correctness without requiring reference answers or repeated sampling. items.title: Generate-then-Rank: Learning Symbolic Goal Interpretation for Embodied Agents
items.one_liner: A two-stage generate-then-rank goal interpretation framework improves symbolic plan generation for embodied AI agents.
items.summary: Goal interpretation translates natural language instructions into formal symbolic goals for embodied agents, where errors propagate across all downstream planning steps. items.one_liner: An analysis of nearly 500k LLM dialogues reveals that explicit URLs appear in only 1.33% of responses, highlighting a gap in inspectable evidence for user checking.

items.title: RIVER: Evidence-guided multi-agent retrieval for enzyme--reaction discovery
items.one_liner: RIVER is an evidence-guided multi-agent framework that uses LLMs and computational tools to improve enzyme-reaction retrieval and function annotation.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced RIVER (Reaction-enzyme Inference via Evidence-guided Retrieval), a multi-agent framework designed for bidirectional enzyme-reaction retrieval. The system coordinates large language models, specialized biochemical computational tools, and external knowledge resources to aggregate multi-level evidence including reaction chemistry, protein sequences, catalytic mechanisms, and database annotations. Validation modules assess evidence gaps and rerank candidates using traceable records. On public benchmarks and E. coli literature retrieval tasks, RIVER outperforms existing general-purpose and biology-specialized multi-agent systems.
items.bottom_line: Evidence-guided multi-agent retrieval frameworks significantly outperform traditional sequence-based models in discovering and annotating enzyme-reaction relationships.

items.title: PCBRouteAgent: How Close Are LLM Agents to Becoming PCB Routing Engineers?
items.one_liner: PCBRouteAgent combines global planning with native tool execution to automate complex printed circuit board routing.
items.summary: Automating printed circuit board (PCB) routing requires coordinating connectivity with strict geometric design rules. Researchers introduced PCBRouteAgent, a multimodal agent combining a Global Routing Planner—which processes board images and electrical information to specify topology, layers, and corridors—with a Detailed Routing Executor that uses KiCad's native engine for local recovery. Evaluated across 247 synthetic and real-world boards from PCBWorld-Bench, PCBRouteAgent achieved clean-pass rates up to 100% on synthetic splits and outperformed existing baselines by wide margins on real-world test subsets.
key_facts: Boards evaluated: 247 synthetic and real-world boards
items.bottom_line: Multimodal LLM agents utilizing decoupled global planning and local recovery can successfully route complex real-world PCBs beyond baseline limits.

items.title: Beneath the Surface: What We Overlook When We Talk About Agent Evolution
items.one_liner: Evaluating agent harness evolution reveals trade-offs in task coverage and cost, leading to the EvoAudit improvement framework.
items.summary: Researchers evaluated agent harness evolution methods for recursive self-improvement without updating model weights across general and coding tasks. Experiments revealed that all sixteen evolved agents gained previously unhandled tasks while losing previously covered ones, with reliability gains often increasing deployment costs. To address these limitations, the authors introduced EvoAudit to revise select, analyze, mutate, and gate mechanisms for improved performance.
items.bottom_line: Recursive self-improvement in agent harnesses without weight updates frequently trades away previously mastered capabilities while increasing compute costs.

items.one_liner: Closed-loop agent evaluation uses versioned rules and dual audit loops to continuously monitor and improve deployed AI agents.
items.summary: Researchers proposed closed-loop agent evaluation, a continuous measurement framework for deployed agents that models evaluation under biased raters and censored outcomes across four analysis levels and execution dimensions. The method utilizes evaluator agents equipped with domain knowledge packs and audit loops to audit evidence, rules, and metrics while driving agent improvement via regression checks. Case studies demonstrate that evidence-and-rule judgment yields higher reliability than holistic scoring.
items.bottom_line: Evidence-and-rule judgment provides significantly higher reliability than holistic scoring when evaluating deployed AI agents.

claims.text: We propose closed-loop evaluation, an evaluation method for deployed agents.
claims.support_span: We propose closed-loop evaluation, an evaluation method for deployed agents.

items.one_liner: TCSExam is a new unified benchmarking framework that evaluates frontier LLMs on theoretical computer science research and open conjectures.
items.summary: Researchers introduced TCSExam, a unified framework and benchmark covering theorem proving, solver engineering, and mathematical constructions to evaluate frontier LLMs on theoretical computer science research. TCSExam-Full contains 100 expert-reviewed tasks with verifications handled by the Lean kernel or executable task checkers, while TCSExam-Lite provides a compact 20-task alternative. Evaluations across multiple agents showed strong alignment between Full and Lite rankings, with GPT-6 Astra and Opus 5.5 leading the indices. The framework provides reproducible tools and Docker recipes to measure progress toward resolving long-standing theoretical conjectures.
items.bottom_line: TCSExam offers a rigorous evaluation framework for tracking LLM capabilities in advanced theoretical computer science and automated mathematical reasoning.

items.summary: Researchers have developed LABBA, a behavioral biometric authentication framework that integrates LLM-based reasoning with phone-blowing acoustic signals. By converting spectral and temporal features into structured prompts, the system achieves high accuracy in both rule-based and score-based modes. This approach addresses limitations in traditional biometric systems, such as poor adaptability to environmental changes and lack of contextual awareness. The framework demonstrated 99.46% accuracy in experiments with 50 participants.
items.bottom_line: Integrating LLMs into behavioral biometrics significantly improves authentication accuracy and robustness against real-world environmental variability.

items.title: The Promise of Strategic Agentic Scambaiting
items.one_liner: A new model shows that defensive AI agents can effectively disrupt scammer operations by out-investing them in mimicry quality.
items.summary: Researchers have developed a formal model to analyze the adversarial dynamics between AI-driven scamming agents and defensive 'scambaiting' agents. The study finds that defensive agents can gain a strategic advantage by prioritizing mimicry quality, which outpaces scammer detection improvements. As baiting-agent prevalence increases, scammer profitability is projected to turn negative, suggesting that autonomous defensive agents are a viable tool for disrupting fraudulent infrastructure.
items.bottom_line: Strategic deployment of defensive AI agents can force scammer profitability into the negative, providing a scalable defense in an AI-mediated fraud landscape.

items.title: Modernising threat hunting: Using Semantic Search to Find Risky AI Agent Behavior
items.one_liner: Semantic vector search over AI agent session logs helps security teams catch risky automated behaviors.
items.summary: Security analysts are exploring vector search and semantic querying over stored AI agent session logs—such as those from Claude Code and Cursor—to detect risky agent behavior that traditional keyword and regex rules miss. Because AI agents dynamically choose actions based on high-level user prompts, individual steps may appear benign while the session as a whole creates security risks, such as accidentally committing sensitive files to public repositories. By embedding interaction turns at ingest and performing semantic similarity searches, teams can flag anomalous workflows for human review without relying on costly per-session LLM evaluations.
items.bottom_line: Vector search over stored AI coding agent sessions enables scalable detection of risky, multi-step agent actions.

claims.text: Semantic search using vector embeddings stored in Elastic allows hunting for risky AI agent sessions.
claims.support_span: In this article, we review using vector search to hunt risky AI sessions. I stored six months of my own Claude Code and Cursor sessions as semantic vectors in Elastic and searched them instead of handing every session to an LLM.

items.title: How I Found a $113,337 AF_ALG Linux Local Privilege Escalation Before Copy Fail
items.one_liner: A retrospective look at uncovering a $113,337 Linux kernel privilege escalation flaw in the AF_ALG cryptographic subsystem via unprivileged socket APIs.
items.summary: Security researcher Muhammad Alifa Ramdhan details the discovery of CVE-2025-39964, a critical race condition vulnerability in the Linux kernel's AF_ALG cryptographic subsystem that earned a $113,337 reward via Google's kernelCTF. Exploiting out-of-bounds access stemming from how AF_ALG handles inputs across unprivileged sockets, an ordinary user can escalate privileges to root or achieve container escape. Present in the kernel since 2011, this vulnerability preceded the widely known 'Copy Fail' flaw but highlights the same underlying kernel attack surface.
items.bottom_line: Unprivileged access to the Linux kernel's AF_ALG subsystem harbors deep race condition vulnerabilities capable of full privilege escalation and container escape.

items.one_liner: Web frameworks like Rails and Spring often overtrust the RFC Forwarded header, leaving applications vulnerable to IP spoofing.
items.summary: Many popular web frameworks and application servers, including Rails, Spring, and Jetty, read values from the RFC 7239 standard Forwarded request header by default. Because reverse proxies and CDNs frequently pass untrusted client-supplied Forwarded headers straight through to backend applications without modification or sanitization, web applications often overtrust the header. This flaw exposes applications to client IP address spoofing, original host name spoofing, and request protocol manipulation. Developers and administrators must configure reverse proxies to drop untrusted proxy headers and ensure their application stack aligns on trusted headers.
items.bottom_line: Failure to strip untrusted Forwarded headers at the reverse proxy layer leaves backend web applications vulnerable to client IP and host header spoofing.

The update that installs the fix still unpacks its files using the site's old, unpatched code, so an attacker who strikes at the right moment can run code on the server. The researcher advises blocking web access to the site's wp-content/upgrade folder before updating. The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-119977, affects WordPress 4.7 through 7.1.3. items.one_liner: GitHub's native egress firewall adds basic network controls, but dedicated tools like Harden-Runner remain essential for cross-platform anomaly detection.
items.summary: GitHub is introducing a native egress firewall for GitHub-hosted Actions runners to bring network controls to builds. While network allowlists are vital for software supply chain security, StepSecurity's Harden-Runner offers broader capabilities that distinguish it from a basic native firewall. Specifically, Harden-Runner supports multiple runner environments including Linux, Windows, and macOS across GitHub-hosted, self-hosted, Kubernetes, and bare-metal servers. It builds automated network baselines from previous runs to detect anomalies, correlates process and file events to specific workflow steps, and provides cross-repository visibility proven against real-world supply chain attacks.
items.bottom_line: Teams relying solely on GitHub's native egress firewall miss critical cross-platform coverage, behavioral baselining, and step-level anomaly detection offered by specialized runtime agents.

items.title: Court acquits DMK leader Ponmudy in ‘derogatory’ religious remarks case after complainant withdraws petition
items.one_liner: Former Tamil Nadu Minister K. Ponmudy was acquitted in a religious remarks case after issuing a public apology and the complainant withdrew the petition.
items.summary: A Metropolitan Magistrate court in George Town has acquitted former Tamil Nadu Minister and DMK leader K. Ponmudy in a criminal case involving alleged derogatory remarks about Shaivism and Vaishnavism. The case stemmed from an April 2025 speech where Mr. Ponmudy allegedly compared religious symbols to sexual positions while narrating an anecdote. Following public outrage and a private complaint filed by BJP councillor Uma Anandan, the leader issued a public apology and expressed personal regret. Consequently, the complainant filed a withdrawal petition, leading the court to acquit Mr. Ponmudy after determining the prosecution failed to prove the charges beyond reasonable doubt.
items.bottom_line: An Indian political leader was acquitted of promoting religious enmity after issuing a public apology that prompted the complainant to withdraw the private petition.
